units.title: Chemistry of Some Nonmetals and Their Compounds

cards.title: 3.1.1 Physical Properties of Nonmetals
body: In their solid state they are generally brittle.
Generally they have low melting and boiling points.

cards.title: 3.1.2 Chemical Properties of Nonmetals
body: Nonmetals are oxidizing agents except carbon which is a reducing agent.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: Carbon monoxide is manufactured in the laboratory by the dehydration of which acid in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid?

steps.text: **Step 1: Identify the laboratory reaction for carbon monoxide**
Carbon monoxide ($$CO$$) is produced by removing water from a simple organic acid.
The reactant is methanoic (formic) acid, HCOOH; concentrated H₂SO₄ removes H₂O from it.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: Which of the following conditions yields the optimum concentration of ammonia ($$NH_3$$) in the industrial Haber-Bosch process?

steps.text: Since there are $$4\text{ moles}$$ of reactant gas and $$2\text{ moles}$$ of product gas, high pressure ($$200\text{ atm}$$) shifts equilibrium to the right.
Since the reaction is exothermic, low temperature shifts it right, but slows the rate.
Industry uses about 200 atm and a moderate temperature of about 450 °C with an iron catalyst: a reasonable yield obtained at a fast enough rate.

cards.answer: High pressure (about 200 atm) and a moderate temperature (about 450 °C) with an iron catalyst

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following nonmetal oxides is completely neutral to litmus paper?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Classify the nonmetal oxides**
$$CO_2$$, $$SO_2$$, and $$NO_2$$ are acidic oxides because they react with water to form acids ($$H_2CO_3$$, $$H_2SO_3$$, and $$HNO_3$$/$$HNO_2$$ respectively).

**Step 2: Identify the neutral oxide**
Carbon monoxide ($$CO$$) is a neutral oxide and does not react with water, acids, or bases to show any pH change.

**Step 3: Final Result**
The neutral oxide is **Carbon monoxide ($$CO$$)**, option **C**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Solid carbon dioxide is commonly referred to in everyday life as:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify solid carbon dioxide properties**
Solid $$CO_2$$ solidifies at temperatures below $$-80^\circ\text{C}$$ and sublimates directly back into gas.

**Step 2: Match with common name**
Because it mimics ice but does not melt into water, it is called "dry ice."

**Step 3: Final Result**
The correct option is **B**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Carbon monoxide is manufactured in the laboratory by the dehydration of which acid in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the laboratory reaction for carbon monoxide**
Carbon monoxide ($$CO$$) is produced by removing water from a simple organic acid.

**Step 2: Recall the chemical equation**
$$HCOOH(aq) \xrightarrow{H_2SO_4} CO(g) + H_2O(l)$$

**Step 3: Identify the reactant**
$$HCOOH$$ is formic acid (methanoic acid).

**Step 4: Final Result**
The correct option is **B**.

cards.title: Nonmetals: general properties
body: Nonmetals are on the right of the periodic table. Most are poor conductors of heat and electricity (graphite is an exception), are brittle when solid, have low melting points (diamond and graphite are exceptions with very high melting points), and tend to gain electrons to form negative ions or share electrons in covalent bonds. Their oxides are usually acidic (e.g. CO₂, SO₂).

cards.title: Carbon and its Compounds
body: **Alloy** = mixture of metals (sometimes with carbon). Harder / stronger / lower melting than the pure metal because the lattice is disrupted.

cards.title: 3.2.1 Carbon
body: Carbon is found in all living things, both plants and animals.
Carbon occurs both in a free and in a combined state.

In its combined state carbon exists as carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, carbonates such as calcium carbonate, and in large quantities as organic compounds, such as hydrocarbons, oils, carbohydrates and proteins.
Allotropes are different forms of the same element that have different physical properties, but generally have the same chemical properties.

cards.title: 3.2.2 Carbon Monoxide
body: Industrially carbon monoxide is manufactured by passing carbon dioxide gas over red-hot charcoal at a temperature about 1000°C.
The concentrated sulphuric acid removes water from the formic acid resulting in the production of carbon monoxide.
Carbon monoxide is a good reducing agent because it removes oxygen during the reaction with reactive metal oxides.
For example, lead oxide is reduced to lead.

cards.title: 3.2.3 Carbon Dioxide
body: Carbon dioxide is a colourless gas which is present in the air in approximately 0.03% by volume.
Human beings inhale oxygen from the air and exhale carbon dioxide.
During photosynthesis, plants use carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and give off oxygen.
Carbon dioxide is an important chemical link between the plant and the animal world.

cards.title: Worked: acid rain link
cards.problem: Why can SO₂ lead to acid rain?

steps.text: SO₂ oxidises and dissolves forming acidic solutions (sulfurous/sulfuric pathways).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Carbon occurs in both crystalline and non-crystalline form which of the following is **crystalline** form?
cards.why:
Carbon has several allotropes:
- **Crystalline forms:** Atoms are arranged in a regular, repeating pattern. Examples: **Diamond**, Graphite, and Fullerenes.
- **Non-crystalline (Amorphous) forms:** No regular pattern. Examples: Coke, Charcoal, and Carbon black.

**Result:** D

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which one of the following is **NOT** true about water gas?

options.C: A mixture of hydrogen and carbon monoxide

cards.why: Water gas is a mixture of **Carbon Monoxide ($$ CO $$)** and **Hydrogen ($$ H_2 $$)**. It is produced by passing steam over red-hot coke. It is highly **combustible** and used as an industrial fuel. Therefore, statement E is false.

cards.title: 3.3.1 Nitrogen
body: Nitrogen is also a constituent element of plant and animal proteins and nucleic acids.
Nitrogen may be obtained in the laboratory by heating a mixture of ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) and sodium nitrite.
The ammonium nitrite that is formed in this reaction is very unstable and is decomposed into water and nitrogen by gentle heating.
Since, nitrogen has a low boiling point, then it is recovered as a gas at the top of the fractionating column.

cards.title: 3.3.2 Ammonia
body: Small quantities of ammonia are found in the atmosphere, in barns, toilets, dung and in the soil.
When an animal and vegetable matter decomposed, much of the protein present in these substances is converted to ammonia.
Nitrogen from the air and hydrogen from natural gas are mixed in the ration of 1:3 by volume.
Nitrogen and hydrogen react at a high temperature and pressure over an iron catalyst.

cards.title: 3.3.3 Nitric Acid and its Compounds
body: Nitric acid is one of the most important inorganic acids.
Laboratory preparation of nitric acid Nitric acid is prepared by heating mixtures of sodium nitrate or potassium nitrate and concentrated sulphuric acid.
The mixture is heated gently and the gaseous nitric acid is given off as a gas.
Pure nitric acid is colourless, but the yellow colour of the distilled nitric acid is due to the dissolved nitrogen dioxide, a reddish brown gas, in the acid.

cards.title: Quick check

options.A: is prepared by the Contact process at industrial level.
options.B: is not used to manufacture explosives.
options.C: is a strong acid and strong reducing agent.
options.D: can be prepared by the reaction between sodium nitrate and concentrated sulphuric acid.

cards.why: In the laboratory, nitric acid ($$HNO_3$$) is prepared by heating a metal nitrate (like **sodium nitrate**) with **concentrated sulphuric acid**. Option A is wrong (Contact process is for $$H_2SO_4$$). Option C is wrong (it's a strong **oxidizing** agent).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which one of the following compounds is most readily used by plants?
cards.why: Plants absorb nitrogen primarily in the form of **nitrate ($$ NO_3^- $$)** and **ammonium ($$ NH_4^+ $$)** ions from the soil. **Ammonium nitrate ($$ NH_4NO_3 $$)** provides both forms, making it a very effective and readily used fertilizer.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following compounds is a **binary** compound?
cards.why:
A binary compound is a chemical compound that contains exactly **two different elements**. 
- Potassium nitrate ($$KNO_3$$): 3 elements.
- Ammonia (**$$NH_3$$**): 2 elements (Nitrogen and Hydrogen).
- Sodium sulphate ($$Na_2SO_4$$): 3 elements.

cards.title: Exam question, solved
cards.problem: Which of the following processes is an industrial preparation of **$$ HNO_3 $$**?  A) Hall’s process  B) Ostwald process  C) Contact process  D) Fountain process  E) Frasch process

steps.text: **Step 1.** The **Ostwald process** is the industrial method used to produce nitric acid ($$ HNO_3 $$) from ammonia ($$ NH_3 $$) through catalytic oxidation.

cards.title: 3.4.1 Sulphur
body: Materials required: Sulphur, carbon disulphide, a glass rod, water, test tubes, a Bunsen burner, glass rods, a watch glass.
What is the colour and odour of the sulphur.
Place the sulphur into a watch glass and crash it with a glass rod.
Sulphur is a bright-yellow non-metallic element.

cards.title: 3.4.2 Sulphur dioxide
body: Sulphur dioxide is prepared in the laboratory by the action of dilute hydrochloric acid on sodium sulphite.
The gas is collected by the down ward displacement of air.
An aqueous solution of sulphur dioxide turns wet blue litmus to red.
In the presence of a catalyst, sulphur dioxide reacts with oxygen to form sulphur trioxide.

cards.title: 3.4.3 Sulphuric Acid
body: The Contact process is the most widely used industrial method for the preparation of sulphuric acid.
The percentage of sulphuric acid produced by this method is high and the acid has a high purity.
Sulphur dioxide is produced by burning sulphur in air.
Since the product contains some impurities, these impurities are removed before the next step.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Industrially, sulphuric acid is prepared by
cards.why: The **Contact process** is the modern industrial method of producing concentrated **sulphuric acid ($$ H_2SO_4 $$)**. It involves the catalytic oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The anhydride of sulphuric acid is
cards.why:
An **acid anhydride** is a non-metal oxide that reacts with water to form an oxyacid. Sulphur trioxide ($$ SO_3 $$) reacts with water to form sulphuric acid ($$ H_2SO_4 $$).

**Reaction:** $$ SO_3 + H_2O \rightarrow H_2SO_4 $$.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: **Contact process** is used for the manufacture of:
cards.why: The **Contact process** is the modern industrial method of producing **sulfuric acid ($$ H_2SO_4 $$)**. It involves the oxidation of sulfur dioxide ($$ SO_2 $$) to sulfur trioxide ($$ SO_3 $$) in the presence of a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst.

cards.title: Exam question, solved
cards.problem: Which of the following is **not** a property of sulphuric acid, $$ H_2SO_4 $$?  A) High density  B) High boiling point  C) Very corrosive  D) Good reducing agent  E) All

steps.text: **Step 1.** Sulphuric acid ($$ H_2SO_4 $$) is a strong **oxidizing agent**, especially when concentrated and hot.
**Step 2.** It is not a reducing agent.
**Step 3.** It is a dense, oily liquid with a high boiling point and is extremely corrosive.

tips.text: Nonmetals are gases, liquids or solids at room temperature. They are bad conductors of heat and electricity. They have usually low boiling and melting points. They are usually electronegative and accept electrons.
Carbon is found in both plants and animals.
Carbon occurs in the free and combined states.
Carbon forms different allotropes because it can take a number of arrangements. However, all the allotropes of carbon are made up only of covalently bonded carbon.
Carbon has two main crystalline forms: diamond and graphite.
The amorphous forms of carbon are the non crystalline forms of carbon.
Charcoal, soot and coke are amorphous forms of carbon.
The different allotropes of carbon have different physical properties.
Carbon burns in oxygen to form carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide. It reduces oxides of zinc and other metals. It also reduces nitric acid and sulphuric acid.
Carbon is insoluble in any of the common solvents. It is also used as an abrasive and graphite is used to make electrodes.

similar.q: Water gas is a mixture of  A) air and water vapour.  B) hydrogen and nitrogen.  C) hydrogen and oxygen.  D) hydrogen and carbon monoxide.  E) nitrogen and carbon monoxide.
similar.a: D. hydrogen and carbon monoxide. — Producer gas is CO + N₂ (E). Answer: D.

similar.a: B. Contact process. — Haber = ammonia; Ostwald = nitric acid; Downs cell = sodium; Hall = aluminium. Answer: B.

similar.a: D. is a reducing agent. — 'Carbon monoxide is a good reducing agent': PbO + CO → Pb + CO₂. Answer: D.

similar.q: When charcoal burns in a limited amount of oxygen, the poisonous gas produced is  A) carbon dioxide.  B) phosphorus pentaoxide.  C) sulphur trioxide.  D) methane.  E) carbon monoxide.
similar.a: E. carbon monoxide. — CO binds to haemoglobin and prevents oxygen transport. Answer: E.

similar.q: It is very risky to stay in a closed room while charcoal is burning because it produces the poisonous gas ______ that causes death.  A) NO₂  B) SO₂  C) CO₂  D) NO  E) CO
similar.a: E. CO — CO combines with haemoglobin much more strongly than oxygen, so blood can no longer carry O₂ – it is colourless, odourless and deadly. Answer: E.

questions.q: A sulphur compound that is used as a bleaching agent is:
why:
**Step 1:** Identify the bleaching properties of sulfur compounds.
**Step 2:** Sulfur dioxide ($$ SO_2 $$) acts as a bleaching agent, especially for delicate materials like wool, silk, and straw.
**Step 3:** Its bleaching action is due to **reduction**, unlike chlorine which bleaches by oxidation. This is why materials bleached by $$ SO_2 $$ may turn yellow again when exposed to air (re-oxidation).
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Which of the following non-metallic oxides is **neutral**?
why: Neutral oxides are those that do not react with either acids or bases. Most non-metallic oxides are acidic (like $$ CO_2, SO_2, SO_3 $$), but a few like CO, NO, and $$ N_2O $$ are neutral.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: One of the following catalyst is useful for industrial preparation of nitric acid?
why:
**Step 1:** Identify the industrial process for Nitric Acid. It is the **Ostwald Process**.
**Step 2:** In the Ostwald process, Ammonia is oxidized to Nitric oxide ($$ NO $$).
**Step 3:** The catalyst used for this reaction is **Platinum (Pt)** or a Platinum-Rhodium alloy gauze.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Dry ice is made by:-
why:
**Step 1:** Define Dry Ice. Dry ice is the solid form of carbon dioxide ($$ CO_2 $$).
**Step 2:** It is produced by cooling and compressing gaseous carbon dioxide until it liquefies, and then allowing it to expand rapidly, which causes it to freeze into a solid state at $$ -78.5^\circ C $$.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: The catalyst used in the manufacture of Nitric acid (Ostwald’s process) is:
why: In the **Ostwald process**, ammonia is oxidized to nitric acid. The catalyst used for the primary oxidation of ammonia to nitric oxide ($$ NO $$) is **Platinum (Pt)** or a Platinum-Rhodium alloy.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Which of the following statements **does not** describe a property of nonmetals?

options.A: Atoms of nonmetals are usually electronegative.
options.B: Oxides of nonmetals are usually acidic.
options.C: Nonmetals do not react with dilute acids.
options.D: Nonmetals donate electrons to form anions.

why: Nonmetals **gain** electrons to form negative ions (**anions**). Donating electrons is a property of **metals** to form cations. Therefore, D is the incorrect statement.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Which one of the following oxides dissolve in water to give a solution that has a pH of less than 7?
why:
**Step 1:** Identify the nature of the oxides. Metal oxides are generally basic, while non-metal oxides are generally acidic.
**Step 2:** Analyze the choices: 
- $$ MgO, Li_2O, K_2O, $$ and $$ Na_2O $$ are metal oxides and form basic solutions ($$ pH > 7 $$).
- $$ SO_2 $$ is a non-metal oxide.
**Step 3:** Reaction of $$ SO_2 $$ with water: $$ SO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow H_2SO_3 $$ (Sulfurous acid).
**Step 4:** Acids have a $$ pH < 7 $$. Therefore, Sulfur dioxide is the correct answer.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: During the dehydration reaction of an alcohol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid, the product is an
why: Dehydration means removing water. When an alcohol (like Ethanol) is heated with concentrated $$H_2SO_4$$, a water molecule is removed, forming a double bond and producing an **alkene** (like Ethene).
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.
